question: Who has been appointed as the Additional Director General (ADG) of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) in August 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sanjeev Raina** was appointed as the Additional Director General (ADG) of the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) in August 2024.
 
• ITBP is a Central Armed Police Force (CAPF) of India that was established primarily to guard the borders between India and Tibet.
 
• The ADG rank is one of the senior-most positions in the ITBP, responsible for overseeing and ensuring operational efficiency and strategic deployment of forces. *Hence, option 1 is correct.*
 
• Sanjeev Raina is a seasoned officer with extensive experience in paramilitary forces and has held various critical positions before this appointment.
 
• The appointment of senior officers in ITBP is crucial, given its strategic role in securing the nation's borders and managing operations in high-altitude terrains.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP):**

 
 
• ITBP was established in 1962 after the Sino-Indian War to guard the Indo-China border along the Himalayan region.
 
• It operates under the Ministry of Home Affairs and is responsible for border security, disaster response, and anti-Naxal operations.
 
• ITBP personnel are specially trained to operate in high-altitude regions and extreme climatic conditions.
 
 
 
• **Role of Additional Director General (ADG):**
 
 
• ADG oversees the operational readiness and administrative functioning of the force.
 
• The role involves coordinating with state and central agencies for border management and law enforcement.
 
• ADG plays a strategic role in modernizing the force and implementing advanced technologies for better surveillance.
 
 
 
• **India-China Border:**
 
 
• The India-China border, also known as the Line of Actual Control (LAC), stretches over 3,488 kilometers.
 
• This region includes difficult terrains like Ladakh, Arunachal Pradesh, and Sikkim, making ITBP's role vital in securing national sovereignty.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Border Security:**
 
 
• The rugged terrain and harsh climate conditions demand specialized training and equipment for personnel.
 
• Frequent tensions along the LAC require constant vigilance and preparedness to handle conflicts diplomatically and tactically.
